purpose: Single source of truth for what 0xDSI can actually do, and how sure we are. Every externally visible claim should map to one entry. The UI must read capability health from here rather than inventing it (wiring is Phase 9). States are an honest Phase-0 snapshot and will move as later phases add tests and integration.

states.implemented: Code exists and runs, but not independently validated against expected outcomes.
states.integrated: Wired end-to-end across its producers/consumers in a running system.
states.validated: Backed by a passing independent test and, where relevant, a benchmark artifact.
states.experimental: Present but unproven or disputed; must not drive automatic action.
states.simulated: Produces synthetic/demo output only; may not populate production evidence.
states.unavailable: Not runnable in the current target (missing engine, hardware, or credentials).

capabilities.title: SOC operator console
capabilities.claim: Analysts view alerts, entities, agents and investigations in one console.
capabilities.notes: Single shipped frontend build. Renders and builds (npm run build passes). Many panels read demo/derived data; per-panel data provenance is a Phase 9 item.

capabilities.title: Backend data API
capabilities.claim: Frontend reads and writes platform data through a governed API.
capabilities.notes: Exposes generic /api/query, /api/mutate, /api/rpc plus typed read endpoints. Generic mutation of protected system-of-record tables is now blocked (Phase 1); reads are not yet authorized. Fail-closed auth and SQL parameterization landed.

capabilities.title: Authorization
capabilities.claim: Every mutation is authorized by role.
blockers: Read-side authorization and agent/notebook tool paths still open
Live SSO role source not verifiable without a real deployment
capabilities.notes: Central authorize() gates generic writes and RPC; roles resolved from a server-side allowlist so the forwarded groups header can no longer escalate; protected system-of-record tables refuse generic writes; response approval enforces separation of duties.

capabilities.title: Threat-intel IOC matching
capabilities.claim: Events are matched against IOCs to raise alerts.
blockers: End-to-end smoke test requires a live Spark workspace (blocked here)
capabilities.notes: Batch matching path exists; live verification blocked in this environment.

capabilities.title: Dempster-Shafer evidence fusion
capabilities.claim: Detector signals are calibrated to threat probability, then fused, with a simple baseline for comparison.
blockers: Per-class base rates are conservative defaults, not fitted from labelled outcomes (needs a live workspace + labels)
capabilities.notes: Raw detector scores are mapped to prior-anchored calibrated probabilities before becoming Dempster-Shafer belief mass (REV2-02/06); the baseline scorer pools one calibrated probability per independence group to avoid double-counting correlated detectors (REV2-03) and is persisted as baseline_score for comparison (REV2-28). Combination math (12 cases) and calibration/baseline invariants (15 cases) pass offline. Stays experimental until base rates are fitted from real outcomes.

capabilities.title: Temporal correlation / complex-event processing
capabilities.claim: Multi-step attack patterns are detected across time with execution scope.
blockers: Native CET engine not pinned/compiled here
capabilities.notes: Bounded matcher approach; the arbitrary-length/standing-query claims and execution-scope binding are Phase 5. Native engine currently unavailable.

capabilities.title: Multi-agent SOC automation
capabilities.claim: Autonomous agents triage, enrich, hunt and respond.
capabilities.notes: Orchestration path exists but many tool responses are simulated. Truthful run lifecycle and 'not_implemented/unavailable' returns are Phase 1.

capabilities.title: Distributed model training (Ray)
capabilities.claim: Models are trained at scale on the platform.
blockers: No Ray cluster / GPU / versioned corpus in this environment
capabilities.notes: Real training, checkpointing and artifact promotion are Phase 7. Must report unavailable, never random scoring.

capabilities.title: Sequence anomaly scoring (MC-RNN)
capabilities.claim: Per-entity behavioral sequences are scored for anomaly.
blockers: Shared featurizer and persisted recurrent state not established
capabilities.notes: Phase 7. Do not label unverified traffic benign by default.

capabilities.title: Source collectors / ingestion
capabilities.claim: Real security telemetry is collected from many sources.
blockers: No Zerobus ingest, no source credentials
capabilities.notes: Per-batch accounting landed (REV2-21): every received record is reconciled to written+quarantined, records that fall through classification are quarantined as unclassified_no_bucket instead of dropped, and a durable ingestion_accounting ledger row is persisted per batch (offline-tested, 11 cases). Real multi-source collection and Zerobus/Delta durability across restarts still need source credentials + a live workspace, so this stays simulated.

capabilities.title: Automated response / containment
capabilities.claim: Approved actions are executed and verified against targets.
blockers: No executor and no controlled test target: execute-time drift enforcement and live target verification need a real workspace and credentials
capabilities.notes: Lifecycle state machine PROPOSED->APPROVED->DISPATCHED->VERIFIED/FAILED (plus REJECTED) with terminal dead-ends keeps a dispatch distinct from a completed action. Approvals are bound to an exact finding revision (REV2-20): approval is refused unless the linked finding is CONFIRMED, the approved revision is recorded, and execution is refused once the finding moves to a new revision or leaves CONFIRMED; separation of duties holds at approve and execute. verify_dispatch marks VERIFIED only when the observed target state matches intent, else FAILED (REV2-27). The server approve endpoint enforces the finding binding and records approved_finding_revision. Logic proven offline (20 property cases). Stays experimental until a live executor and target are available.

capabilities.title: Natural-language data questions
capabilities.claim: Operators ask questions in plain language over platform data.
capabilities.notes: Backed by a real language-model query path (relabeled honestly from an earlier overstated 'native' claim).

capabilities.title: Finding-revision lifecycle
capabilities.claim: A finding's state changes are recorded as an immutable, validated revision chain.
blockers: Only the alert-dedup job emits revisions so far; primary detection writers do not yet open findings as PROVISIONAL revisions
Append-only durability across restarts needs a live Delta workspace to verify
capabilities.notes: Immutable PROVISIONAL->CONFIRMED/WITHDRAWN/EXPIRED/SUPERSEDED state machine with a fixed transition table (terminal states are dead ends, re-confirm rejected); every revision is append-only and stamped with the five execution-identity fields (REV2-05). Logic proven offline (13 property cases). Persisted to the finding_revisions ledger.

capabilities.title: Replay-safe evidence writes
capabilities.claim: Re-running an evidence producer never duplicates the evidence it already wrote.
blockers: Insert-if-absent MERGE and cross-table atomic commit need a live Delta workspace to verify at runtime
capabilities.notes: Deterministic, content-addressed keys (injective over part boundaries, None distinct from empty) plus an insert-if-absent MERGE in safe_append(idempotency_key=...) make evidence writes replay-safe (REV2-04). Wired into UEO objects (ueo_id), UEO signals (signal_id) and forensic collections (collection_id); the same change fixed a latent crash where four agents passed an idempotency_key argument the function did not accept. stamp_execution_identity provides the REV2-05 identity kernel for evidence rows. Key/stamp logic proven offline (12 property cases). Stays experimental until the MERGE path is exercised on a live workspace.

capabilities.title: Leakage-safe evaluation and promotion gate
capabilities.claim: A model is measured without leakage and only promoted to serving when it beats a baseline and is not overfit.
blockers: Real labelled corpus, trained artifacts and a live Ray/Spark workspace needed to run the gate on actual models
capabilities.notes: Leakage-safe splitting (temporal split with the boundary timestamp kept whole; grouped split so an entity never spans train and test; leakage_keys proves a split is clean), rank-based ROC-AUC and precision/recall/F1, and a promotion_gate that refuses a model below an AUC floor, without a margin over the 0.5 baseline, overfit (train-minus-test gap too large), or measured on a single-class slice (REV2-14, REV2-28 model side). The threat-scoring notebook now uses a temporal split instead of a leaky randomSplit and gates registration and production scoring on the decision. Logic proven offline (17 property cases). Stays experimental until run against real trained artifacts.

capabilities.title: Fail-closed audit trail for privileged mutations
capabilities.claim: A privileged change is recorded before it happens, or it is refused.
blockers: Exercising the journal fallback and the 503 refusal against a live warehouse needs a real Databricks SQL endpoint
capabilities.notes: REV2-29: the prior audit path swallowed every exception, so a privileged mutation could run unrecorded. audit.py now builds a complete attributable record (rejecting one missing operation/table), persists it to the primary system_audit_log or, on failure, to a durable append-only local journal (flushed + fsync'd), and raises only when both sinks fail. The server audits write-ahead on every privileged mutation (generic write, RPC, response approval) and returns 503 to refuse the action when audit cannot be persisted; a primary failure absorbed by the journal is logged, never silent. Logic proven offline (10 property cases). Stays experimental until the fallback and refusal paths are exercised on a live warehouse.

capabilities.title: Readiness that never reports a false green
capabilities.claim: The service reports ready only when its dependencies actually answer.
blockers: Hard driver-level timeout enforcement and a downstream canary need a live Databricks SQL endpoint
capabilities.notes: REV2-25: the prior /ready probe reported ready as soon as a connection handle existed, so a STARTING warehouse (which accepts a handle) read as ready. readiness.py classifies a bounded SELECT 1 canary -- only the expected answer inside the time budget is READY; STARTING, TIMEOUT (budget overrun) and FAILED (error or wrong answer) are distinct non-ready states -- and aggregate_readiness is deny-by-default, granting readiness only when every required dependency is READY (an empty or all-optional set is not a vacuous green). The /ready endpoint runs the canary, returns per-dependency states, and answers 503 until truly ready. Logic proven offline (15 property cases). Stays experimental until run against a live warehouse.
